chunks: And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Temporary marriage (al-mut'ah) was mentioned to him, and he was asked: Is it one of the four [types of marriage]? He said: 'Marry a thousand of them, for they are hired women.'

key_terms.مُسْتَأْجَرَاتٌ: Hired women (referring to the nature of Mut'ah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on temporary marriage (Mut'ah) in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) explicitly validates temporary marriage (al-mut'ah) as a legitimate form of union, distinguishing it from permanent marriage by characterizing the participants as 'hired' (musta'jirat) for a fixed term. This narration underscores the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence regarding marital contracts, emphasizing that the contractual nature of mut'ah allows for multiple concurrent unions, thereby facilitating social and personal needs without the permanent binding obligations of standard nikah.
